The 6 Dimensions of Freight Data Quality

10 min read Updated: November 2026 By Rajvardhan Singh Rathore
While general data quality frameworks define six abstract dimensions, logistics systems require concrete mathematical formulas and physical boundary rules. This guide operationalizes each dimension for transportation data pipelines.

Logistics Data Quality Dimensions Matrix

Dimension Freight Definition Failure Example Target SLA
Completeness Availability of all required shipment manifest fields Missing consignee postal code or carrier SCAC > 99.8%
Accuracy Degree to which digital record matches physical truth Recorded weight 150 kg, actual scale ticket 1500 kg > 99.5%
Consistency Harmony across multimodal status records and ERPs WMS says 'SHIPPED' but Carrier API returns 'UNKNOWN' > 99.0%
Timeliness Time elapsed between physical event and digital ingestion Delivery milestone ingested 36 hours post-handover < 15 min lag
Uniqueness Absence of duplicate event or billing entries Carrier webhook retries causing duplicate PU scans 100.0%
Validity Adherence to domain schemas, enums and regex standards Invalid ISO-8601 date '11/12/2026 2pm' > 99.9%

1. Completeness

In freight ETL pipelines, completeness is measured as a field-level and record-level ratio:

$$ ext{Completeness Rate} = rac{\sum_{i=1}^{N} ext{Non-Null Mandatory Attributes}}{N imes ext{Total Required Attributes}} imes 100$$

Mandatory freight keys include master_shipment_id, carrier_code, service_tier, origin_location_code, and destination_location_code.

2. Accuracy

Accuracy verifies digital claims against physical ground truth. For example, geofencing coordinates from trailer GPS pings must fall within the polygon radius of the specified logistics terminal:

PostGIS SQL 
-- Assert event GPS is within 500 meters of reported terminal hub
SELECT 
  e.event_id,
  e.shipment_id,
  ST_Distance(
    ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(e.longitude, e.latitude), 4326)::geography,
    h.geofence_center::geography
  ) AS distance_meters
FROM stg_tracking_events e
JOIN dim_logistics_hubs h ON e.reported_hub_code = h.hub_code
WHERE ST_Distance(
  ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(e.longitude, e.latitude), 4326)::geography,
  h.geofence_center::geography
) > 500;

3. Consistency

Ensures that multiple reporting systems tell the same story. In intermodal freight (rail + truck + ocean), state machines must progress monotonically without conflicting terminal statuses.

4. Timeliness

Calculates the ingestion latency quantile ($p_{95}, p_{99}$):

$$ ext{Latency} = t_{ ext{ingested\_at}} - t_{ ext{event\_occurred\_at}}$$

Late-arriving facts corrupt dynamic routing algorithms and trigger erroneous customer SLA breach penalties.

5. Uniqueness

Guarantees idempotency. Carrier HTTP webhook retries must never generate duplicate billing entries or double-counted delivery events in the enterprise data warehouse.

6. Validity

Strict schema syntax adherence: tracking numbers must pass standard carrier checksum algorithms (such as UPS Modulo-10 or ISO 6346 container check digits), and timestamps must follow ISO-8601 UTC format.

Computing the Composite Data Quality Score (DQS)

Enterprise logistics platforms combine the 6 dimensions into a weighted score:

$$ ext{DQS} = 0.25 C_{ ext{comp}} + 0.25 A_{ ext{acc}} + 0.15 K_{ ext{cons}} + 0.15 T_{ ext{time}} + 0.10 U_{ ext{uniq}} + 0.10 V_{ ext{valid}}$$
